PullRequest.Title: EXP integration id pass-through via body
PullRequest.Body:

* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Adds the configured integration ID as `userParams.integratorid` in TAS assignment request bodies for VS Code core and Copilot Chat, using the existing audience-filter providers.

Unlike #345739, this does not add an HTTP header or change legacy requests, avoiding the CORS regression. Also removes misleading comments claiming the core transport bypasses renderer CORS.

Adds the necessary filter while resolving the problems mentioned in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/10641

Scenarios.Scenario: VS Code core treatment initialization for signed-in and signed-out windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The assignment service constructs the existing TAS client and its initial fetch; callers can consume cached treatments while network initialization is pending, while a cold uncached treatment may wait for client initialization/fetch. The diff only adds one constant userParams entry before the existing assignments POST.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST the serialized assignment userParams through IRequestService to the account-specific TAS endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing assignments POST for the selected signed-in endpoint per initial/refetch cycle; the payload gains one small constant field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same POST occurred with the same scheduling and endpoint, but without the integratorid JSON property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing cold assignment retrieval can await this request; warm cached treatment reads can progress before it completes. The added field does not add another boundary or await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover/reuse a signed-out TAS host and POST the same assignment body.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request with a remembered healthy host; on cold discovery or failure, up to three existing staggered endpoint attempts, with losers cancelled after success.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical discovery/failover calls and concurrency, with a body lacking integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold signed-out assignment retrieval already depended on discovery; the one extra constant JSON field does not change attempt count, staggering, timeout, or cancellation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate AssignmentsFilters and serialize userParams into the existing TAS request body.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional Map entry and one additional bounded JSON property per existing request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Enumerated and serialized nine assignment filter names instead of ten.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds constant-size CPU/allocation work only; it does not scale with product data or block on an external resource.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dynamically load the existing tas-client module before constructing the client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per TAS client generation, unchanged by the added filter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same module load occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing setup boundary; the new imported constant and filter entry do not introduce or repeat module loading.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write the existing persistent TAS memento around assignment results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing storage access per client/result lifecycle; no added access from integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same memento lifecycle occurred without integratorid in the network body.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Storage behavior remains unchanged and is not multiplied by the added request-body field.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One VS Code window/client generation and one bounded filter map; the added effective cardinality is exactly one key/value pair per existing assignments request, independent of workspace size, treatment count, or extension count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Signed-in routing retains one existing assignments request per fetch cycle. Signed-out discovery retains the existing staggered hedging behavior: normally one remembered endpoint, with up to three endpoint attempts during cold discovery/failure. The diff adds no task, queue, retry, or concurrency source.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persistent TAS memento behavior and warm cached-treatment reads are unchanged. The assignments request still disables transport caching and follows the existing initial/refetch lifecycle; the new constant does not alter cache keys or add positive/negative cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: changed lines add only an enum member/switch return, and traced callers serialize the existing filter map into the same existing request path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Backend targeting may intentionally change which assignments are returned for a configured integration ID, but the diff supplies no evidence that response size or latency grows; code-side overhead is a fixed short string pair.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The code adds constant bounded serialization/allocation without changing boundary count, cache behavior, critical-path placement, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: VS Code core hourly refresh and account/filter-triggered client replacement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing coalesced refetch waits for initialFetch and one TAS refresh call; account identity changes may replace the client and start the existing generation's fetch. The added static filter participates in every existing body but does not trigger filter-change events or replacement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh TAS treatments using the existing client and assignment request path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced refetch in flight per service, normally once per hour; one constant property is added to each existing assignments payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same refetch frequency, coalescing, and requests occurred without integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This background refresh is off ordinary UI critical paths; explicit consumers waiting for refreshed data retain the same network dependency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return the static integration ID while rebuilding the existing filter map for a request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(1) additional lookup/string reference per request; no collection-dependent work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Negligible bounded local work before the existing request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Refresh frequency is hourly plus existing account/filter changes; effective request multiplicity remains one coalesced refetch at a time per window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: refetchPromise continues to coalesce overlapping requests; client generations are revoked/disposed on replacement. No new concurrent generation or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing persistent memento remains shared across generations, stale generations are revoked, and refetch scheduling is unchanged. The static integrator value has no invalidation or negative-cache lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the refetchPromise coalescing, hourly scheduler, generation revocation, and static provider implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual account/filter change frequency varies, but the changed work is fixed per already-existing request and cannot amplify event frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; no repeated boundary, missing coalescing, or concurrency burst is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot Chat experimentation initialization and refresh for signed-in or signed-out users
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Delegate creation snapshots the existing assignment filter map, then the TAS client performs its existing initial network fetch; hasTreatments waits for initialization/initialFetch. Hourly refresh and delegate recreation on authentication/routing changes are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform the existing signed-in assignments POST through IFetcherService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing assignment request per client fetch cycle; one small constant property is added to its JSON body.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same endpoint call occurred without integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: hasTreatments may wait for the existing initial fetch; the diff neither adds another request nor moves it onto this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST to a preferred signed-out TAS endpoint or discover one with staggered failover.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call when a preferred endpoint works; up to three existing endpoint attempts on cold discovery/failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical signed-out fan-out and endpoint preference with no integratorid body field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing signed-out initialization can wait up to the established timeout; the added JSON field does not change hedging, retries, cancellation, or timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Add the constant integration ID to the existing Map and serialize it in assignment userParams.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one bounded Map entry/property per existing filter snapshot/request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The filter map and body contained one fewer constant property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant local CPU/allocation before the existing fetch; no unbounded metadata is copied or encoded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read product.json once when constructing the existing assignment filter provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per service/provider construction, unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same product.json read already occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pre-existing constructor work; importing INTEGRATION_ID does not introduce another filesystem read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and update existing persisted experimentation state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-delegate/result storage lifecycle, unchanged by the added field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same memento accesses occurred without integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Warm memento reads can serve existing data; no storage operation is added or repeated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One added constant Map entry per delegate snapshot/request. Frequency remains initial activation, hourly refresh, and existing authentication/routing changes; it does not scale with chats, messages, treatments, or token organization count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Signed-in behavior retains the existing single endpoint path. Signed-out discovery retains one preferred call or up to three staggered attempts during discovery/failure. Delegate generation revocation and disposal remain unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing extension Memento supplies warm state and retains its three-day/version validity checks. The integration ID does not alter memento keys, cache invalidation, endpoint preference, or failure caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the provider is snapshotted into the existing TAS configuration, network adapters and timers are unchanged, and the only runtime addition is a constant Map entry.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The backend may use the new intended targeting input to return different assignments, but no repository evidence establishes a larger response or slower operation. Local overhead is fixed and tiny.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression. Boundary fan-out, polling, cache lifecycle, and critical-path waits are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all six changed files and traced both VS Code core and Copilot Chat assignment flows through serialization, client setup, caching, network routing, signed-out endpoint discovery, periodic refresh, coalescing, generation replacement, and persistence. The PR adds one bounded constant userParams property to existing request bodies; it introduces no additional I/O, network call, retry, polling event, retained lifecycle, or concurrency.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
